g.text: The wrong qualifying rate can create a false pass.

text.style: font-size: 10px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #54635e

g.text: Worked audit: Vancouver, two earners, price 10% lower (CAD 764,100), CAD 150,000 gross income, unchanged purchase cash.

text.style: font-size: 8px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; fill: #54635e

g.text: Each incorrect row introduces one deliberate calculation error; the cash position is held fixed. The correct qualifying rate uses the contract rate

text.style: font-size: 8px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; fill: #54635e

g.text: plus 2 percentage points or 5.25%, whichever is higher. A false pass means the flawed calculation fits both checks while the correct one does not.

text.style: font-size: 8px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; fill: #54635e

g.text: These are defined examples, not observed errors at TD or any other lender, and not a bank error-rate estimate. Sources: CMHC debt-service guidance and

text.style: font-size: 8px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; fill: #54635e
